title: Hydrogel Arrays Enable Increased Throughput for Screening Effects of Matrix Components and Therapeutics in 3D Tumor Models
protocol: Prepare HEPES-buffered solution by dissolving HEPES powder at 20 mM in Hank's balanced salt solution (HBSS).
Adjust pH to 7 following full solvation.

In the HEPES-buffered solution, dissolve thiolated HA (700 kDa nominal molecular weight) so that 6%-8% of carboxylic acid residues on each glucuronic acid are modified with a thiol at a concentration of 10 mg/mL in buffer solution.
Stir using a magnetic stir plate (<1,000 rpm) at room temperature until fully dissolved, typically around 45 min.

Prepare separate solutions of (1) 100 mg/mL of 8-arm-PEG-Norbornene (20 kDa), (2) 100 mg/mL of 4-arm-PEG-Thiol (20 kDa), (3) 4 mM of cysteine or cysteine-containing peptide, and (4) 4 mg/mL of LAP in microcentrifuge tubes.
Vortex each solution to ensure full dissolution of the reagent.
Mix the individual solutions of HA, PEG-Norbornene, PEG-thiol, and cysteine/thiol-containing peptides to achieve final concentrations for hydrogel matrices.
Stir the mixture (<1,000 rpm) on a magnetic stir plate for at least 30 min to mix fully.
Download the Illumination Device.zip file from the Supplementary Coding Files.
Install the microcontroller software (see Table of Materials).
Install the GUI software (see Table of Materials).
Open Processing and install the controlIP5 library via Sketch > Import Library > Add Library.
Search for controlIP5 in libraries and click on Install.
Power the illumination device using the 36 Volt power supply.
Connect the illumination device to a PC using a micro-USB cable.
Open the Arduino.ino file using Arduino IDE.
Compile the Arduino.ino file by clicking on the Checkmark button.
Upload the compiled code by clicking on the Arrow button.
Open the GUI.pde file using Processing.
Click on Run in the processing program to launch the graphical user interface.
In the graphical user interface window, click on Intensity for the column containing hydrogel precursor solution and input the desired intensity.
Input 15 s in the Time box.
Align the samples with the illumination device with every other LED in a single column of the silicone molds or 384-well plate.
Click on Finish to begin illumination.
Move the well plate to the next corner after illumination for the first set of wells.
Lift the plate out of the holder and rotate 180° to illuminate wells on the other half of the plate.
Clean the glass slides and silicone molds using tape to remove debris.
Adhere the silicone molds to the glass slide, press down to ensure a good seal, and displace any air bubbles.
Pipette 80 µL of hydrogel precursor solution into each silicone mold on the glass slide.
Place the glass slide onto the illumination device aligned with every other LED in a single column.
Expose the hydrogel precursors to UV light for 15 s to photocrosslink.
Retrieve the slides once illumination has stopped.
Loosen the gels from the molds by tracing the inner circumference of the mold with a fine tip.
Remove silicone molds with tweezers/forceps.
Move crosslinked hydrogels into individual wells of a 12-well plate using a wet spatula and gently pushing them off the glass slide.
Fill each well with 2 mL of DPBS prior to adding the hydrogel.
Swell the gels in DPBS solution for at least 12 h at room temperature.
Turn on the atomic force microscope (AFM) according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Install the AFM probe.
Align the laser to the apex of the triangular probe.
Adjust mirror and laser deflection to maximize signal sum between 1.5-2.2 Volts.
Immerse the probe in DPBS and wait up to 15 min for thermal equilibrium.
Click on the Calibration button and select Contact-Dependent calibration.
Click on the Collect Thermal Tuning button.
Select the peak around 3 kHz for calibration after data collection.
Approach the surface of a Petri dish by setting parameters to Constant Velocity, target height of 7.5 µm, and approach speed of 15 µm/s.
Enable Baseline Measurement Per Run for Approach.
Set acquisition parameters for force mapping to 4 nN turnarounds, 2 µm indentation distance, 1 µm/s velocity, and 0 s contact time.
Press the Start button to begin collecting a force curve on the plastic surface.
Return to the calibration window.
Select the portion of the force curve corresponding to contact and indentation of the plastic.
Accept the calculated sensitivity and stiffness values for the probe.
Raise the AFM probe.
Place the hydrogel sample for interrogation.
Approach the hydrogel following the settings provided in step 5.
Obtain a force curve as in step 4.6 if the unit mistakenly triggers the approached state during approach procedure.
Repeat the approach procedure if the resulting curve does not show contact and resulting indentation.
Switch to the Force Mapping mode when the surface approach is successful.
Set acquisition parameters to a map of 8 x 8 size with 40 µm length per axis.
Obtain force maps in various regions to assess the uniformity of stiffness measurements.
Interpret force curves using the software program JPK SPM Data Processing through a Hertz/Sneddon model fit with spherical geometry selected.
Collect GBM spheroids from a T-75 flask suspension culture into a 15 mL conical tube.
Rinse the culture flask with 5 mL of DPBS and add this volume to the conical tube.
Centrifuge the conical tube containing cells at 200 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant using a 5 mL serological pipette, taking care not to disturb the cell pellet.
Resuspend in 5 mL of DPBS and centrifuge at 200 x g for 5 min at room temperature to wash cells.
Aspirate the supernatant with a 5 mL serological pipette, taking care not to disturb the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 2 mL of cell dissociation reagent.
Incubate at room temperature for 10-15 min.
Add 3 mL of complete medium and gently pipette 3-5 times to break down spheroids into a single-cell suspension.
Centrifuge the single-cell suspension at 400 x g for 5 min to pellet cells at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant with a 5 mL serological pipette, taking care not to disturb the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of complete medium.
Pass cells through a 40 µm cell strainer if they remain in clumps after passaging.
Remove a portion of the cells for counting using a hemocytometer.
Dilute this portion two-fold with trypan blue.
Count only live, colorless cells.
Spin down cells at 400 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant with a micropipette.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the hydrogel precursor solution by pipetting up and down 4-5 times.
Prime the repeat pipettor by dispensing an additional 1-2 times into a waste container to avoid bubbles.
Dispense 10 µL of cells suspended in hydrogel solution into each well of a 384-well plate using the repeat pipettor.
Illuminate each well containing cells for 15 s with intensities ranging from 1.14, 1.55, 2.15 to 2.74 mW/cm².
Add 40 µL of complete media to each well containing the cells.
Add 50 µL of DPBS to non-experimental, dry wells surrounding the gels.
For GBM cells, add 40 µL of the media-containing drug to achieve the final desired concentration starting 3 days after encapsulation.
Add 10 μL of CCK8 reagent to each well containing the cells.
Incubate for 1-4 hours according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Read absorbances at 450 nm for all wells following incubation.
